ask.title: 8 questions to ask a software company when getting a quote
ask.intro: When collecting quotes from software companies in Ankara, ask for written answers to these questions. A quote with unclear answers means surprise costs during the project.
ask.i1: Is the scope written out screen by screen, and how is out-of-scope work priced?
ask.i2: Is payment split into stages (a deposit and delivery milestones)?
ask.i3: When are the source code, database and documentation handed over?

softwareFirmPage.q10: What should a software contract include?
softwareFirmPage.a10: The scope (list of screens and features), the total price and staged payment plan, the delivery schedule, acceptance criteria, when the source code will be handed over, in whose name the domain and server accounts will be opened, support and maintenance terms, and KVKK clauses. faq.title: Spam update penalty: frequently asked questions
faq.q1: Why have my clicks from Google suddenly dropped to zero?
faq.a1: The most common reason is that Google has pushed your site down in search results after a spam update, or has applied a manual action to your site. First check the “Security & Manual Actions” section in Search Console; if there is a notice there, you have a manual action. If there is no notice but the drop matches the date of an update announced by Google, an automatic effect may be the cause. An exact diagnosis requires looking at traffic and page data together.
faq.q2: How much does spam update recovery cost?
faq.a2: Diagnosis and cleanup costs 75,000–120,000 TL (3–6 weeks), full recovery 120,000–180,000 TL (6–10 weeks), and recovery combined with SEO and GEO work 180,000–280,000 TL (10–16 weeks). The initial assessment is free.
faq.q3: When will my traffic come back?
faq.a3: With a manual action, a reconsideration request is usually answered within a few days to a few weeks. With automatic drops, it can take several months for Google's systems to notice the changes. A return to the old traffic level is not certain either; traffic that came from low-quality pages in particular may not come back.
faq.q4: Do you guarantee to bring back my old traffic?
faq.a4: No. Nobody can guarantee Google's decision. We diagnose the problem accurately, clean up everything that breaches the policies and report on the process in writing every month.
faq.q5: Is a disavow file always necessary?
faq.a5: No. Google already ignores most bad links. A disavow file is mainly needed if you received a manual action because of links, or if you have many links that were knowingly bought. Because a badly prepared file can also harm your useful links, we prepare it with care.
faq.q6: Would moving to a new domain solve the problem?
faq.a6: Usually not. If the problem is in the content, you will get the same result on the new domain and lose everything your old domain had built up. Fixing the problem first is almost always the better path.
faq.q7: Why is my site not showing on Google?
faq.a7: There can be several reasons a site does not show on Google: the site was accidentally blocked from search engines (a noindex or robots.txt mistake), server errors, a hack, or a Google penalty. The “Pages” and “Manual actions” reports in Search Console usually point to the cause; we go through them together in the free initial assessment.
faq.q8: How do I remove a Google penalty?
faq.a8: With a manual action, you first fully fix the problem Google pointed out, then send a reconsideration request through Search Console explaining the fixes you made. With an automatic drop there is nowhere to apply; you clean up the problem and wait for Google to reassess the site. In both cases, the most important step is finding the real source of the problem.

faq.a2: For 2026, a website KVKK and security audit costs 30,000–60,000 TL, an audit of an AI-connected web or mobile app 60,000–120,000 TL, and an audit combined with fixes 120,000–250,000+ TL. The price depends on the number of forms, pages and systems; we give the exact price in a written quote after the discovery call. There is no monthly fee for the audit.
faq.q3: Is it a problem to use Google Analytics without cookie consent?
faq.a3: Analytics and advertising cookies are not considered strictly necessary, so they are generally expected not to run before the user consents. What we check technically is whether these tags really stay off before consent, whether the "reject" option works and whether consent is recorded. Ozturksoft uses the same approach on its own site: analytics cookies do not run before consent and a consent record is kept (our cookie and KVKK notice). The legal assessment for your site should come from your lawyer.
faq.q4: What should I do if the forms on my site send data to AI?
faq.a4: First you need to know which data goes to which service (such as OpenAI, Google Gemini or Anthropic Claude) and to which country; we map this in the audit. We then suggest steps such as stripping unnecessary personal data before sending, informing users on the form and asking for explicit consent where needed; you finalise the wording with your lawyer. If the data must not leave the country at all, running the AI on your own on-premise server is also an option.
faq.q5: How long does the audit take?
faq.a5: A website audit usually takes 1–2 weeks, and an audit of an AI-connected web or mobile app 2–4 weeks. If the audit and fixes are done together, the total is 3–6 weeks. The timeline also depends on how quickly access (live site, source code, database) is provided.
faq.q6: Do you also provide legal advice?
faq.a6: No; we are a software team and our work is a technical compliance and security audit. We recommend finalising the wording of the privacy notice and consent texts, and whether VERBİS registration is required, with a lawyer. Our report sets out clearly the technical facts your lawyer needs for these decisions (which data goes where, where it is stored, who can see it).
faq.q7: Will you make the fixes after the audit?
faq.a7: Yes, if you want. When you take the audit and fixes together, the work costs 120,000–250,000+ TL and takes 3–6 weeks; we fix cookie consent, consent records, encryption, access rules and permissions, then re-check. You can also hand the report to your own team; for ongoing checks, our maintenance and support service is 5,000–10,000 TL per month.
faq.a8: A simple brochure site with no forms, no visitor tracking, no ad tags and no personal data collection usually does not need a full audit; a short check is enough. If that is your situation, we will tell you so openly in the discovery call. If you have forms, accounts, payments, an AI connection or an app that stores customer data, an audit makes sense.
faq.q9: Is KVKK mandatory for a website?
faq.a9: If your site has a contact form, membership, orders, analytics cookies or ad tracking that process personal data, KVKK duties to inform users and, where needed, obtain explicit consent apply. A simple brochure site with no forms or tracking has more limited obligations. We recommend clarifying the required texts with your lawyer and checking the technical side with us.
faq.q10: What should cookie consent look like?
faq.a10: Non-essential cookies (analytics, advertising) should not run before the user consents; accepting and rejecting should be equally easy, and users should be able to change their choice later. In the audit we technically test whether these cookies load before consent. We use the same approach on our own website.
faq.q11: What should mobile apps watch out for under KVKK?
faq.a11: The permissions the app requests (location, camera, contacts) should be genuinely needed and explained to the user, and the privacy notice should be reachable inside the app and on the store page. In the audit we check which data the analytics and advertising libraries send where, and how personal data is stored on the device and the server.
